payload.summary: A change that WEAKENS a clinical safety guard living under tests/ escapes the governance preflight gate, because the gate has no pattern for the tests that are the guard
payload.detail: Found by the clinical-governance-reviewer while reviewing PR #2521 on 2026-09-02; recorded rather than fixed there, because it is not that PR's to fix. scripts/pr-policy.mjs decides whether a PR must carry a completed '## Clinical Governance Preflight' by matching changed paths against clinicalRiskPatterns, which covers src/lib/*clinical*, src/app/api/, supabase/, src/data/ and similar. It has no pattern for tests/**. But several of this repository's clinical safety guards ARE tests: tests/caring-contacts-interface-vocabulary.test.ts is the only software check on prohibited wording across five source trees; tests/helpers/caring-contacts-prohibited-language.ts is the single shared definition of that vocabulary; tests/caring-contacts-overlay-definitions.test.ts holds the 24 frozen overlay rows against docs/caring-contacts/interaction-matrix.md; and the Ruling [143] parity block is what stops the message-side 'lead' rule drifting looser than the screen's. PR #2521 was classified clinicalRisk:false and correctly so by the letter of the rule -- it touches only tests/** and docs/outstanding-issues-inbox/**. The asymmetry is that the SAME paths would carry a PR that deletes a scan root, widens an exemption from one literal to a whole file, relaxes the 'lead' lookbehind, or removes the parity block, and pr-policy would wave every one of those through with no preflight and no reviewer prompted to look for clinical consequences. The gate is direction-blind: it cannot tell strengthening a guard from removing one, because it reads paths and not intent. Worth noting the near miss that makes this concrete rather than theoretical: PR #2521's own first draft exempted src/lib/caring-contacts/message-rules.ts as a whole file, which would have put the five sentences a discharged patient reads by SMS permanently outside the scan. A subagent review caught it. Nothing in the required checks would have. Candidate fixes, in increasing cost: add the specific guard test files to clinicalRiskPatterns by name, which is cheap and precise but needs maintaining as guards are added; or add tests/** paths that import CARING_CONTACTS_PROHIBITED_LANGUAGE or the message rules, which is self-maintaining but needs an import scan in pr-policy; or a narrower gate that only fires when such a file's diff is net-deleting. Prefer whichever keeps a false positive cheap, since the cost of a wrong classification here is one preflight section a human fills in, and the cost of the current gap is an unreviewed weakening of a patient-facing safety guard.
